original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-equiv-fibre-product}
For a scheme $X$ denote $|X|$ the underlying set.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Then
$$
|X \times_S X| \to |X| \times_{|S|} |X|
$$
is surjective.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, let $|X|$ and $|S|$ denote the sets of topological points. The natural map $|X\times_S X|\to|X|\times_{|S|}|X|$, taking a point of the fibre product to its two projections, is surjective.
stage_b_review_note: Retains surjectivity on underlying POINT SETS of |X×_S X|→|X|×_|S||X| for arbitrary scheme f:X→S, with no claim of homeomorphism or pointwise uniqueness.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, let $|X|$ and $|S|$ denote the sets of topological points. The natural map $|X\times_S X|\to|X|\times_{|S|}|X|$, taking a point of the fibre product to its two projections, is surjective.
hypotheses: f:X→S is any morphism of schemes.
conclusions: Any pair of points of X with the same image in S lifts to a point of X×_S X.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. For any family of scheme maps $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}$, if it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes, then the induced map of underlying topological spaces $\coprod_i|X_i|\to|X|$ is surjective. Likewise, if $X$ and every $X_i$ are affine and the family is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of affine schemes, then $\coprod_i|X_i|\to|X|$ is surjective.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves both sufficient conclusions that universal effective epimorphism families in schemes or affine schemes are jointly surjective on points, respecting the affineness restriction of the second clause.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. For any family of scheme maps $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}$, if it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes, then the induced map of underlying topological spaces $\coprod_i|X_i|\to|X|$ is surjective. Likewise, if $X$ and every $X_i$ are affine and the family is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of affine schemes, then $\coprod_i|X_i|\to|X|$ is surjective.
hypotheses: Family is a universal effective epimorphism in schemes, or in affines when all terms affine.
conclusions: The family is jointly surjective on underlying points.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-check-universal-effective-epimorphism-affine}
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms of schemes.
If for every morphism $Y \to X$ with $Y$ affine the family of base changes
$g_i : Y_i \to Y$ forms an effective epimorphism, then
the family of $f_i$ forms a universal effective epimorphism
in the category of schemes.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. Let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a family of morphisms of schemes. Suppose that for every morphism $Y\to X$ with $Y$ an affine scheme, the base-changed family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism in the category of schemes: compatible maps from its members to any test scheme glue uniquely to a map from $Y$. Then the original family is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes (with no affineness restriction on base change $Y\to X$).
stage_b_review_note: Preserves checking universal effective epimorphism in schemes after every AFFINE base change Y→X, with no requirement that every X_i or original X be affine. The descent of gluing across arbitrary Y is the conclusion.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. Let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a family of morphisms of schemes. Suppose that for every morphism $Y\to X$ with $Y$ an affine scheme, the base-changed family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism in the category of schemes: compatible maps from its members to any test scheme glue uniquely to a map from $Y$. Then the original family is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes (with no affineness restriction on base change $Y\to X$).
hypotheses: All affine base changes of the family are effective epimorphisms of schemes.
conclusions: The family is universally an effective epimorphism in schemes.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-open-fpqc-covering}
Let $\{f_i : T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be a fpqc covering.
Suppose that for each $i$ we have an open subset $W_i \subset T_i$
such that for all $i, j \in I$ we have
$\text{pr}_0^{-1}(W_i) = \text{pr}_1^{-1}(W_j)$ as open
subsets of $T_i \times_T T_j$. Then there exists a unique open subset
$W \subset T$ such that $W_i = f_i^{-1}(W)$ for each $i$.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $\{f_i:T_i\to T\}$ be an fpqc covering of a scheme $T$ and choose an open subset $W_i\subseteq T_i$ for each $i$. Suppose that for every pair $(i,j)$ the inverse images $\operatorname{pr}_0^{-1}(W_i)$ and $\operatorname{pr}_1^{-1}(W_j)$ in $T_i\times_TT_j$ coincide. Then there exists a unique open subset $W\subseteq T$ such that $W_i=f_i^{-1}(W)$ for all $i$.
stage_b_review_note: Retains fpqc descent of open subsets W_i on covering T_i with exact equality of their pullbacks to all T_i×_T T_j, yielding one unique open W⊂T and W_i=f_i^{-1}W. Full cocycle equality and uniqueness are retained.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $\{f_i:T_i\to T\}$ be an fpqc covering of a scheme $T$ and choose an open subset $W_i\subseteq T_i$ for each $i$. Suppose that for every pair $(i,j)$ the inverse images $\operatorname{pr}_0^{-1}(W_i)$ and $\operatorname{pr}_1^{-1}(W_j)$ in $T_i\times_TT_j$ coincide. Then there exists a unique open subset $W\subseteq T$ such that $W_i=f_i^{-1}(W)$ for all $i$.
hypotheses: fpqc covering, compatible open subsets on the cover and all pairwise overlaps.
conclusions: Compatible open subsets descend uniquely to an open subset of T.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms}
Let $\{T_i \to T\}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Then $\{T_i \to T\}$ is a universal effective epimorphism
in the category of schemes, see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-universal-effective-epimorphisms}.
In other words, every representable functor on the category of schemes
satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-sheaf-property-fpqc}.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. If $\{T_i\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering of a scheme $T$, then it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes. Equivalently, for every base change $T'\to T$ and every test scheme $Z$, every family of maps $h_i:T_i\times_TT'\to Z$ whose restrictions agree on all pairwise fibre products $(T_i\times_TT')\times_{T'}(T_j\times_TT')$ comes from a unique map $h:T'\to Z$. Thus every representable presheaf $\operatorname{Hom}(-,Z)$ on schemes satisfies fpqc descent.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves that every fpqc covering is a universal effective epimorphism in SCHEMES, equivalently every representable functor Hom(-,Z) satisfies fpqc sheaf descent after any base change. Uniqueness of glued morphism maintained.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. If $\{T_i\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering of a scheme $T$, then it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes. Equivalently, for every base change $T'\to T$ and every test scheme $Z$, every family of maps $h_i:T_i\times_TT'\to Z$ whose restrictions agree on all pairwise fibre products $(T_i\times_TT')\times_{T'}(T_j\times_TT')$ comes from a unique map $h:T'\to Z$. Thus every representable presheaf $\operatorname{Hom}(-,Z)$ on schemes satisfies fpqc descent.
hypotheses: The family is fpqc, with arbitrary base change and target test scheme.
conclusions: The family is a universally effective epimorphism; representable functors are fpqc sheaves.
